nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Margo Rivera was an accountant. She kept the books for half the harbour, from a small office in town.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: It's shut now. The blinds are down. Through the gap you can see her desk, squared to the millimetre, the way she left it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I've asked round. Nobody can tell me what she was like at that desk. The people who paid her knew her numbers. That's all they knew.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: A listener wrote to me this week. She swam for the county with Margo when they were both fifteen.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: She says Margo could outswim the other three. Liam, Ruby, Brad. Any of them, any day.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: And when people in Havenbay watched her stand on the slip with a flask while the others went in, she let them think what they liked. She never corrected anyone.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Violet painted her office door, years back. Charged her about half what it was worth, because Violet did that.

nodes.speaker: Liam Bryce
nodes.line: Margo worked out the real price and posted her a cheque for the difference. With a note. Don't be a martyr, it said.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: That was fourteen years ago. They were friends from that day.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Every Tuesday Violet left a bag of receipts at Margo's office. Loose, in a carrier bag, for sorting.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Every Friday she collected it, untouched. Margo did the sorting herself. Every week.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Ruby says it had been a joke between them once. Violet's bag. I don't know when it stopped being funny.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Here's what her last months look like from the outside. After the sixth meeting at Ruby's table, Margo stopped arguing. She still came. She sat, and she didn't say much.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: After Brad went, she pulled away from Ruby. Fewer calls, then none. Ruby says her edges got sharper. Short with people who didn't deserve it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: And every second Sunday she drove somewhere. Nobody knew where. Nobody who asked got an answer.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: That's all I have. A silence, but it has a shape.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: A listener went back to the public record this week, and read something I'd read a dozen times without stopping.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Violet's neighbour at number 14 told police, on the day Violet was found, that she'd seen a man in the lane behind Violet's house the night before. About half past ten.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: His back to her, going out the back way. A coat. Hands empty. No more than that.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: That's been in the record for nine months. Nobody was hiding it. It just sat there.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The listener set the neighbour's description of his build against Liam Bryce. Liam is a big man. Anyone in Havenbay would tell you that.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: So the listener's question is this. Was the man in the lane the wrong build for Liam? I'm putting it to you exactly as it was put to me. I don't have the answer.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Margo was ten minutes early to everything. Always ten. Not five, not fifteen. Ruby says she'd sit in the car until the hour and then walk in on the minute.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Her car was found at Kestrel Head, the headland car park where Brad left his. The dashboard clock read ten minutes before eleven.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Ten minutes early. She went to that car park the way she went everywhere.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I don't know what that means. I know it's her. That's as far as I can take it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I've written this next part down, because I want to get it right and not add to it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Margo Rivera. In the months before she died. Did she say anything, to anyone. About the letter, about Brad, about the four of them. About anything at all.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: A sentence in a car park. Something at a till. Something she started and didn't finish. If she said it to you, write to me. Not to anyone else. Write to me.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: One more thing about Margo, from Ruby.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: Since the funeral she made me cry twice. Both times she was right. Both times she said it the worst way a person could say it.

nodes.speaker: Ruby Walker
nodes.line: She apologised for one of them. For the way she'd said it. She didn't take back a word of it, and she was right not to.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Episode five went out on the Tuesday. The question about Margo went out with it, word for word, the way I wrote it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Then three days of nothing. Not nothing, exactly. Her dry cleaner wrote in. She paid on time and liked her collars stiff. Two people told me she was polite.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: That's what you get when you ask a city about a private woman. You get her dry cleaner. Nobody wrote to say what she thought. Maybe nobody knows.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: That's the halfway mark of this season. The question stands, and I'll keep asking it. Write to me, not to anyone else. This is Echoes of Havenbay, I'm Ally Quinn. Goodnight for now, Harbour. Sleep tight.
